source_row.rationale: Breast self-awareness (being familiar with one's own normal breast tissue and promptly reporting any new changes) can support early recognition of potential concerns, but current guidance generally positions this as a complement to, not a replacement for, clinical breast exams and appropriate screening mammography per age/risk-based guidelines, since self-exam alone has not been shown to reduce breast cancer mortality on its own.
source_row.source_detail: Role of Breast Self-Awareness Alongside Clinical Screening
source_row.source_name: American Cancer Society — Breast Awareness and Screening Guidance
source_row.stem: A nurse is providing health promotion education about breast health, and a client assumes that once they've had a mammogram, there's really no further reason to also pay attention to their own breast tissue between screenings.
